content.figure_caption: Recommended default antithrombotic therapy regimens in acute coronary syndrome patients without an indication for oral anticoagulation.

summary.choice_of_P2Y12_inhibitor: For ACS, prasugrel or ticagrelor preferred; clopidogrel recommended if prasugrel and ticagrelor are unavailable, contraindicated, or not tolerated (Class I). When proceeding to PCI prasugrel > ticagrelor (Class IIa).
summary.P2Y12_pretreatment_in_NSTE-ACS: Routine pretreatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor in NSTE-ACS patients in whom coronary anatomy is not known and early invasive management (<24 h) is planned is not recommended. Pretreatment may be considered in NSTE-ACS patients not expected to undergo early invasive strategy (<24 h) and who do not have high bleeding risk.
summary.anticoagulation_choices: Various anticoagulants listed by scenario (UFH, enoxaparin, bivalirudin, fondaparinux) depending on STEMI vs NSTE-ACS and timing of angiography.

footnotes_highlights: Fondaparinux (plus a single bolus of UFH at the time of PCI) is recommended in preference to enoxaparin for NSTE-ACS patients in cases of medical treatment or logistical constraints for transfer to PCI within 24 h of symptom onset.

Routine pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor in NSTE-ACS patients in whom coronary anatomy is not known and early invasive management (<24 h) is planned is not recommended; pre-treatment may be considered in patients not expected to undergo early invasive strategy and without high bleeding risk.

Clopidogrel is recommended for 12 months DAPT if prasugrel and ticagrelor are not available, cannot be tolerated, or are contraindicated; may be considered in older ACS patients (typically >70–80 years).

genes.context: The guideline repeatedly refers to 'P2Y12 receptor inhibitor' and guidance on pretreatment and choice of P2Y12 inhibitor (e.g., routine DAPT: aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor; recommendations regarding pretreatment in NSTE-ACS and choice among prasugrel/ticagrelor/clopidogrel).
